author: KawzInvests
zh: KawzInvests指出token需求一個月翻倍、GPU租價上升，顯示算力需求強勁。
text:
Token demand just doubled in a month, and it did that while token prices were falling by half. 
Over the same stretch, the cost of locking in the GPUs that actually produce those tokens has gone up.

- Tokens: OpenRouter processed 113 trillion last week. 25x in a year, 2x in the last month.

- Token price: Silicon Data's index printed 97 cents per million, less than half the June peak.

- GPU price: Silicon Data's H100 index is $2.53 today, up from $2.00 in December. SemiAnalysis's one year contract series ran from $1.70 last October to about $2.80 in July. B200 is $5.64.

Think of a bakery with a limited number of ovens. The bakers learn to bake five times as many loaves per hour, so bread gets cheap and the town eats more of it. That does not make ovens cheap. Everyone wants one now, so oven rent goes up while bread goes down. Bread is tokens, ovens are GPUs.

I have seen the token price chart going around all week and it is missing some key context. Cheaper tokens on their own could mean a glut or a shortage, but nobody with idle GPUs raises rent, so what it actually shows is the cost of producing a token coming down while the compute that produces it stays scarce. We are still short on compute.

U.S. memory maker Micron plans to double its high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production capacity from last year. Through aggressive capital spending by year-end, the company aims to strengthen its supply capabilities for 12-high HBM4, the latest generation of HBM. The move is intended to increase its market share by expanding its HBM capacity, which currently trails that of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on September 3, Micron plans to add up to 60,000 wafers per month of HBM production capacity by the end of this year. The net addition would exceed the company’s HBM production level of roughly 40,000–50,000 wafers per month last year.

“Micron is making substantial investments in equipment to rapidly ramp up its HBM4 production capacity,” said an industry source familiar with the matter. “By the end of this year, it will have secured HBM production capacity of approximately 100,000 wafers per month.”

To achieve this expansion, Micron is increasing purchase orders (POs) with multiple HBM equipment suppliers. Equipment deliveries are understood to be ongoing at its HBM manufacturing sites in Taiwan and Singapore.

The share of 12-high HBM4 in Micron’s production mix is expected to rise significantly. Currently, 12-high HBM3E accounts for most of its HBM output. As recently as early this year, 12-high HBM4 represented only 20–30% of the total, but that share is reportedly set to reach as much as 50% by year-end.

Twelve-high HBM4 will be used in Vera Rubin, the latest AI accelerator from NVIDIA, the world’s largest AI chip company. Micron began mass production of its 12-high HBM4 products in the second quarter of this year.

【美股复盘 · 9月4日】

受非农就业数据及美国10年期国债收益率攀升至4.8%等宏观因素拖累，美股大市整体受压。标普(

个股焦点方面，特斯拉(TSLA)全日重挫5.90%，沦为表现最差的权重蓝筹之一。消息面上，其即将推出的Cybercab因移除方向盘设计而面临监管部门严格审查，市场忧虑其自动驾驶(Robotaxi)愿景落地受阻，引发资金抛售。另一方面，市场传出重磅内部人士大手吸纳消息，据SEC披露文件显示，另类资产机构Sixth Street掌门人Alan Waxman按28.78美元作价，自掏腰包买入逾4780万美元自家信贷基金股份，巨额真金白银入市，引发市场高度关注。

小结而言，当前美股盘面呈现出强烈的结构性割裂。宏观层面受制于高债息压制，传统避险与估值修复逻辑持续角力；惟另一边厢，具备实质业务支撑的硬件及存储板块则持续吸纳资金。分析指，在息率前景明朗化之前，大市料维持反复上落格局，资金或进一步向确定性较高的科技硬件龙头集中，后市宜密切留意国债收益率走势及重磅科技股之承接力。

Micron, Semiconductor Substrate Makers Show Interest in JDI's Mobara Plant Sale

Japanese display maker Japan Display Inc. (JDI) has drawn interest in the sale of its Mobara plant (fab), which halted operations this March, not only from Micron of the United States and several data center operators but also from a semiconductor substrate maker, according to sources on the 8th.

The JDI Mobara plant previously produced sixth generation liquid crystal displays (LCD) and organic light emitting diodes (OLED). It also mass produced OLED panels for the Apple Watch until the second half of 2025. As JDI had announced in the first quarter of 2025, it halted operations at Mobara in March 2026.

Industry source A said, "Micron and several data center operators have submitted letters of intent to JDI to acquire the Mobara plant." Another source B said, "Micron and a Korean semiconductor substrate maker, among others, are in talks with JDI over purchasing the Mobara plant." At its quarterly earnings announcement in early August, JDI stated that it was in discussions with multiple companies regarding the sale of the plant.

The reason Micron, data center operators, and semiconductor substrate makers are interested in the Mobara plant comes down to time. Building a new plant from scratch and securing government permits would take years before mass production could begin. Buying the Mobara plant shortens that timeline accordingly.

Because Mobara previously produced sixth generation LCD and OLED panels, its cleanroom cleanliness levels make it unsuitable for semiconductor front end processing, but the site can be used as a data center or as a back end packaging plant for products such as glass substrates. That is why Micron, data center operators, and substrate makers are interested. The sale price for the plant is currently reported to be under discussion at around KRW 500 billion, though the figure could change depending on circumstances.

OLEDWorks, a US OLED company working with JDI, is reported to be interested not in the Mobara plant but in the 4.5 generation Ishikawa plant. Ishikawa has a line capable of backplane (BP) processing. For OLEDWorks, securing a plant that can reliably handle BP processing going forward is a necessity.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Qualcomm Form 2.1D Packaging Alliance, Jointly Developing an "Organic Bridge" That Bypasses Intel's EMIB

Samsung Electro-Mechanics is teaming up with Qualcomm to develop "organic bridge" technology for advanced packaging of artificial intelligence (AI) chips. Beyond Qualcomm, Samsung Electro-Mechanics is also co-developing organic bridge technology with several other customers in parallel.

An organic bridge is similar to the silicon bridge used in Intel's EMIB (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge) packaging, but it uses organic materials, the kind commonly found in printed circuit boards (PCBs), instead of silicon.

According to industry sources on the 14th, Samsung Electro-Mechanics is jointly developing organic bridge technology with Qualcomm for use in 2.1D packaging. Development and validation work has been under way for more than a year. The evaluation involves embedding an organic bridge into a flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrate that connects Qualcomm chips, and then assessing the substrate's performance and reliability.

Qualcomm is understood to be considering the organic bridge for large multi-die chips for data centers, among other applications. In October 2024, the company filed a patent for an "Interconnect Bridge" technology, in which a separately fabricated organic material based bridge is embedded in a package substrate to connect multiple dies. In March this year, Qualcomm also hired organic bridge personnel in Korea.

An organic bridge is a component that connects multiple semiconductor dies integrated in a single package. It can be thought of as an ultra small substrate with ultra fine circuitry. It is made by forming multiple layers of fine circuits on an organic dielectric using a redistribution layer (RDL) process. Because it enables finer wiring than the build-up circuitry of a conventional FC-BGA, it can carry more signals across a smaller area. Jefferies latest report is just the latest example of how the BOM is shifting massively from the GPU toward memory and then interconnect.

In today's GB300 NVL72, the GPU is 62.5% of the rack and networking just 8.6%. By the Rubin Ultra NVL576 pod, the GPU falls to 46% and networking climbs to 22.4%, because once you link eight racks into a single 576-GPU domain, the interconnect between them becomes part of the computer itself.

Rubin Ultra NVL576 lands in the second half of 2027, and that's where networking takes over: CPO debuts in H2 2027 and scales from there. But remember, the market looks 6 to 12 months ahead, so the interconnect trade starts well before then.

Memory and pluggables are the present, CPO is the future, and the rack tells us where the money goes.

Third, a key part of ZeroFlap’s moat is the Pilot software layer.

Looking into FY28 and beyond, Credo is entering Near Package Optics, or NPO, for scale-up AI networks, where connection density is 10 times higher.

zh: Ren：六年前的A100仍保有約25%價值，反駁GPU兩三年就沒價值的空頭論點。
text:
$NVDA
 
$NBIS


The biggest bear case on AI infrastructure has been that GPUs lose their value in two or three years, so everyone building data centers is overstating their earnings. This chart puts real prices on that argument.

Using Silicon Data's pricing, a six-year-old A100 still holds about 25% of its purchase price, which is where an accelerated depreciation schedule expects it to be at year two. An H100, four years after mass availability, is still worth 58%. And a B200 is trading at 158% of what it cost, a sign of how far demand is running ahead of supply.

That changes the math for everyone who owns compute. If a GPU is still worth more than half its price after four years, a five or six-year depreciation schedule starts to look conservative.

The neoclouds benefit the most, because GPUs are their collateral, their balance sheet and their product all at once, so every point of residual value makes financing cheaper and returns higher.

The honest caveat: it's Nvidia's own chart, the purchase prices are third-party estimates, and a B200 above 100% is a shortage price that won't last forever. But even the oldest chip on the chart is beating the bear case by four years.

Old compute keeps getting put back to work, and that's one of the strongest arguments for the whole buildout.

We are crushing the bears over here

zh: Ren：退休帳戶最大持倉是Google，擁有最多AI層，卻仍被當成會被AI取代的搜尋公司定價。
text:
$GOOGL
 

Most people don't know this, but in my retirement account, my biggest position by far is Google.

Alphabet owns more layers of the AI stack than any other company, and it's still priced like the search business everyone thought AI would kill.

Search grew 17% last quarter to $63.3B, so the "AI kills Google" story still hasn't shown up in the numbers. Below that sit Gemini and DeepMind at the model layer, then Google Cloud, which grew 82% to $24.8B while its operating margin jumped from 20.7% to 35.6% in a year. And at the bottom, Google designs its own chips, and it's now signing deals to supply multiple gigawatts of TPUs to other companies.

Cloud backlog reached $514B, up more than $50B in a single quarter, with just over half expected to turn into revenue within two years. That's roughly $257B already signed for the next 24 months, against a Cloud business running at about $99B a year today.

The price for all of it is about 22x forward earnings, below Microsoft at 25x, while growing faster. Ignore the 17x you'll see quoted everywhere, because it's inflated by a $98B gain on Alphabet's investment portfolio.

Capex guidance is now $195 to $205B for this year and set to rise significantly in 2027, and they raised $80B in equity in June to help pay for it, so you're buying a company that spends like a utility to grow like a startup.

It's hard to bet against a company this integrated across the whole stack. The one thing missing is a spark at the model layer, where Google has fallen behind OpenAI and Anthropic this year, and Gemini 4 might be exactly what lights it.

zh: Michael Sikand：美光財報後市場相信週期不會在2027見頂，但懼怕總經不給高本益比；管理層稱漲價速度已見頂。
text:
After 
$MU
 earnings, it's clear the market believes the cycle won't peak in 2027 but is too fearful of the macro to award memory the multiple to match.

The stock is roughly flat after hours even after management said the pace of price hikes has peaked. 

While management says prices for memory will keep rising, they will do so at a "more moderate rate". Revenue and margins are still estimated to rise every quarter of 2027.

Memory stocks have always traded on rate of change, so it looks like the reaction reads as acceptance of a new framing around the industry.

That new framing? It's built on visibility we have never seen before in the sector. 

Customers have signed $150B in long term contracts with price floors, and these deals are expected to make up over 35% of Micron's revenue through 2030. At those floor prices, Micron expects margins above any peak memory cycle before it.

That's absolutley insane so let me repeat. 1/3 of Micron's revenue through 2030 is visible to us as investors at huge margins. It is extremely rare to have this level of long-term visibility into a business, especially one built on booms and busts.

While this is extremely bullish, the stock isn't moving because the entire AI trade is interconnected and investors are struggling to assess long term viability.

This visibility depends on the buyers of the memory being able to meet their commitments. Currently the macro picture is very bleak. Surging yields and rate hikes could make it harder for AI companies to keep buying memory, more and more of which is being paid for with debt. The Fed just hiked in September and the 10 year Treasury yield is hitting its highest level in 20+ years.

Overall, if the memory trade is to make its next leg up towards a more structural multiple, the macro picture must improve primarily with de-escalation in Iran.

zh: Ren：認同高盛「AI成為選股市場」觀點，AI交易分化是最利多的事。
text:

I had the chance to check out Goldman Sachs' "AI Is Becoming a Stock Picker's Market" and I agree with most of what's being shared.

The AI trade stopped being one trade, and that's the most bullish thing that could happen to it.

Since 2023-2024 you could buy anything with AI in the deck and it went up with everything else.

This summer was different. Half of the ten biggest tech names were up and the other half were down, and Nasdaq multiples have compressed about 20% this year with the 10-year above 5.25%.

That is what a maturing cycle looks like. 

When multiples stop expanding, earnings have to do the work, and earnings are where this trade is strongest this Q. 
$MU
 just guided to $61.5B for a single quarter, lead times across the supply chain are still stretching, and semis trade at a discount to the S&P.

A market that moves together rewards being early, and we've had plenty of that over the last year.But that phase is mostly gone. 

A market that splits apart rewards knowing where the bottleneck is, layer by layer, and which companies get paid when it tightens. 

Not all companies are created equal, and we are seeing big dispersion between them.

A year ago the easy money was just owning the right theme. Now it goes to the right companies within each theme, and to knowing what sets them apart.
